title: Drop the redundant channel_posts_recent_idx (write-amplification cleanup)

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: loopctl operator carrying the coordination bus at platform volume
story.i_want_to: remove the now-redundant recent-reads index that the hardening migration superseded but never dropped
story.so_that: every channel_posts write maintains one recency btree instead of two overlapping ones — no wasted write amplification or bloat

rationale: The design panel's architect flagged a real shipped bug: the create migration (20260717020000_create_channel_posts.exs:37-39) added `channel_posts_recent_idx` on `(tenant_id, project_id, inserted_at DESC)`; the hardening migration (20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs:34-36) added `channel_posts_recent_seq_idx` on `(tenant_id, project_id, inserted_at DESC, seq DESC)` — a strict SUPERSET that serves every query the old index served — but never dropped the old one. Both are plain btrees, so every insert now maintains two overlapping indexes. On a bus that takes a post per session-turn across a fleet this is pure write amplification and bloat with zero read benefit. This is the zero-risk first step in the re-scope sequencing.

background.reference: priv/repo/migrations/20260717020000_create_channel_posts.exs:37-39 (old index); priv/repo/migrations/20260718000000_harden_channel_posts_slot_and_ordering.exs:34-36 (superseding index); panel finding 'Redundant index (real shipped bug)'.
background.includes: A forward-only cleanup migration that drops the superseded index; the recent-reads path keeps using channel_posts_recent_seq_idx, which order_recent/2 (coordination.ex) already targets.

acceptance_criteria.description: A new cleanup migration drops `channel_posts_recent_idx` (the index created at 20260717020000_create_channel_posts.exs:37-39). After migrate, `\d channel_posts` (or an information_schema/pg_indexes query) shows `channel_posts_recent_seq_idx` present and `channel_posts_recent_idx` absent.

The migration is idempotent-safe for already-migrated and fresh environments: `drop_if_exists index(..., name: :channel_posts_recent_idx)` so a fresh DB that never had the old index (were the create migration ever consolidated) does not fail. `down/0` recreates `channel_posts_recent_idx` exactly as the create migration declared it, so the migration is reversible.

No code change to coordination.ex is required: recent_page/3 (coordination.ex) already orders by `inserted_at DESC, seq DESC` (order_recent/2 non-delta clause, coordination.ex), which is served by `channel_posts_recent_seq_idx`. The read path is verified unchanged (existing US-39.3 read tests stay green).

test_cases.name: old index is gone after migrate
recent read still returns newest-first
preconditions: several posts with same-microsecond inserted_at, differing seq
expected_results: ordering is inserted_at DESC then seq DESC — identical to pre-migration behavior

technical_notes: Pure DDL cleanup — no schema/context change. Add priv/repo/migrations/<ts>_drop_redundant_channel_posts_recent_idx.exs.
down/0: recreate it exactly as 20260717020000_create_channel_posts.exs:37-39 (same columns, same name) for reversibility.
Do NOT touch channel_posts_recent_seq_idx (the keeper) or channel_posts_session_key_uidx. seq is read_after_writes (channel_post.ex:90); the seq index is the sole recency btree after this.
Zero-risk, do FIRST in the sequencing — it de-risks the busier read/write changes that follow by shrinking the write path.
